literal: Geography Treatise IV: Nanjing Circuit
idiomatic: Geography Treatise IV — Nanjing Circuit

literal: Nanjing Xijin Prefecture—in ancient times the land of Ji.
idiomatic: Xijin Prefecture at Nanjing was the old territory of Ji.

literal: Gaoyang called it Youling; Taotang Youdu; Shun divided out Youzhou.
idiomatic: The Gaoyang era knew it as Youling; Yao as Youdu; Shun carved out Youzhou.

literal: Shang merged You into Ji.
idiomatic: Under Shang, You was folded into Ji.

literal: Zhou divided and rejoined as You.
idiomatic: Zhou reorganized the region once more as You.

literal: Offices of Region: northeast Youzhou; mountain cult Yiwulü; marsh Mo yang; rivers He, Cuo; soaking Zi, Shi.
idiomatic: The Offices of Region record northeast Youzhou with cult mountain Yiwulü, marsh Mo yang, rivers He and Cuo, and the Zi and Shi soaking-in lands.

literal: Products fish and salt; livestock horses, cattle, swine; grains millet, panicum, rice.
idiomatic: Its staples were fish and salt; its herds horses, cattle, and pigs; its grains millet, panicum, and rice.

literal: King Wu enfeoffed Grand Guardian Shi in Yan.
idiomatic: King Wu enfeoffed the Grand Guardian Shi in Yan.

literal: Qin made the territory five commanderies: Yuyang, Shanggu, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong.
idiomatic: Qin organized the region into Yuyang, Shanggu, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, and Liaodong commanderies.

literal: Han made it the State of Yan, successively enfeoffing Zang Tu, Lu Wan, Liu Jian, Liu Ze, Liu Dan; at times Zhuo Commandery and Guangyang State were placed here.
idiomatic: Under Han it became the State of Yan, held in turn by Zang Tu, Lu Wan, Liu Jian, Liu Ze, and Liu Dan, with Zhuo Commandery and Guangyang State established at intervals.

literal: Later Han made Guangping State and Guangyang Commandery, sometimes merged into Shanggu, then Youzhou was restored.
idiomatic: Later Han assigned Guangping State and Guangyang Commandery, at times joined to Shanggu; Youzhou was set up again.

literal: Later Zhou placed Yan and Fanyang commanderies; Sui made Youzhou a grand protectorate.
idiomatic: Later Zhou created Yan and Fanyang commanderies; Sui made Youzhou a grand protectorate.

literal: Tang placed a metropolitan grand protectorate and changed it to the Fanyang military commissioner.
idiomatic: Tang installed a metropolitan grand protectorate, later the Fanyang military governor.

literal: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Cong, Liu Ji seized the region in succession.
idiomatic: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Cong, and Liu Ji carved it out one after another.

literal: Liu Zong submitted to Tang.
idiomatic: Liu Zong returned to Tang allegiance.

literal: Through Zhang Zhongwu and Zhang Yunzhong righteousness won the people.
idiomatic: Under Zhang Zhongwu and Zhang Yunzhong upright rule won the populace.

literal: Father and son Liu Rengong contended in usurpation, and the region passed into the Five Dynasties.
idiomatic: Liu Rengong and his son fought in mutual usurpation until the land entered the Five Dynasties era.

literal: From Tang into Jin, Gaozu, for Liao aid in enthroning him, ceded Youzhou and fifteen other prefectures.
idiomatic: When Tang gave way to Jin, Gaozu rewarded Liao for supporting his accession by ceding Youzhou and the other fifteen prefectures.

literal: Taizong raised it to Nanjing, also called Yanjing.
idiomatic: Taizong promoted it to Nanjing, also styled Yanjing.

literal: Changping County.
idiomatic: Changping County.

literal: Originally Han Jundu County; Later Han belonged to Guangyang Commandery; Jin to Yan State; Northern Wei set Eastern Yan Prefecture, Pingchang Commandery, and Changping County.
idiomatic: It was Han Jundu County; Later Han Guangyang Commandery; Jin Yan State; Northern Wei founded Eastern Yan Prefecture, Pingchang Commandery, and Changping County.

literal: Commandery abolished; county subordinated to Youzhou.
idiomatic: When the commandery was abolished the county answered to Youzhou.

literal: Ninety li north of the capital.
idiomatic: It lay ninety li north of the capital.

literal: Seven thousand households.
idiomatic: Seven thousand registered households.

literal: Lu County.
idiomatic: Lu County.

literal: Originally a Han county, belonging to Yuyang Commandery.
idiomatic: Formerly a Han county in Yuyang Commandery.

literal: Tang Wude year 2 set Yuan Prefecture; Zhenguan year 1 the prefecture was abolished and it again became a county.
idiomatic: Tang Wude year 2 created Yuan Prefecture; in Zhenguan year 1 the prefecture was abolished and the county restored.

literal: There is the Lu River.
idiomatic: The Lu River flows there.

literal: Sixty li east of the capital.
idiomatic: It stood sixty li east of the capital.

literal: Six thousand households.
idiomatic: Six thousand registered households.

literal: Anji County.
idiomatic: Anji County.

literal: Originally a Han county, belonging to Yuyang Commandery.
idiomatic: Formerly a Han county in Yuyang Commandery.

literal: Tang Wude year 4 moved fifty li southeast to Shiliang walled town; Zhenguan year 8 again moved five li west of the present county to Changdao walled town; Kaiyuan year 23 again moved south of Gengjiu Bridge market.
idiomatic: In Tang Wude year 4 the seat shifted fifty li southeast to Shiliang town; Zhenguan year 8 to Changdao town five li west of the present site; Kaiyuan year 23 to the market south of Gengjiu Bridge.

literal: One hundred twenty li south of the capital.
idiomatic: It lay one hundred twenty li south of the capital.

literal: Twelve thousand households.
idiomatic: Twelve thousand registered households.

literal: Yongqing County.
idiomatic: Yongqing County.

literal: Originally Han Yichang County; Sui set Tongze County; Tang set Wulong County, renamed Huichang; at the start of Tianbao it became Yongqing County.
idiomatic: It was Han Yichang County; Sui Tongze County; Tang Wulong, then Huichang; at the opening of Tianbao it was renamed Yongqing.

literal: One hundred fifty li south of the capital.
idiomatic: It stood one hundred fifty li south of the capital.

literal: Five thousand households.
idiomatic: Five thousand registered households.

literal: Wuqing County.
idiomatic: Wuqing County.

literal: Former Han Yongnu County, belonging to Yuyang Commandery.
idiomatic: Former Han Yongnu County in Yuyang Commandery.

literal: Commentary on the Water Classic: Yongnu is the name of a marsh-lake; water on four sides is yong; water that does not flow is nu.
idiomatic: The Water Classic commentary explains Yongnu as a marsh name: water on four sides is yong; stagnant water is nu.

literal: At the start of Tang Tianbao it was changed to Wuqing.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tang Tianbao it was renamed Wuqing.

literal: One hundred fifty li southeast of the capital.
idiomatic: It lay one hundred fifty li southeast of the capital.

literal: Ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

literal: Xianghe County.
idiomatic: Xianghe County.

literal: Originally Sun Village in Wuqing.
idiomatic: Formerly Sun Village in Wuqing.

literal: Liao placed a salt monopoly office at Xincang; residents gathered; households were split from Wuqing, Sanhe, and Lu counties to establish it.
idiomatic: The Liao founded a salt monopoly at Xincang; settlers clustered there, and households were carved from Wuqing, Sanhe, and Lu to form the county.

literal: One hundred twenty li southeast of the capital.
idiomatic: It stood one hundred twenty li southeast of the capital.

literal: Seven thousand households.
idiomatic: Seven thousand registered households.

literal: Yuhe County.
idiomatic: Yuhe County.

literal: Originally Quanshan territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Quanshan land.

literal: Liu Rengong built palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain; the master Wang Ruone taught elixir and ascension arts to the court; Jixian was split off to supply them.
idiomatic: Liu Rengong erected palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain; Wang Ruone instructed the court in alchemy; a portion of Jixian was detached to provision them.

literal: Forty li west of the capital.
idiomatic: It lay forty li west of the capital.

literal: One thousand households.
idiomatic: One thousand registered households.

literal: Huoyin County.
idiomatic: Huoyin County.

literal: Originally Huo Village in Han Quanshan.
idiomatic: Formerly Huo Village in Han Quanshan.

literal: Each spring Liao hunted at Yanfang Marsh; residents formed a town; the old Huoyin walled town was walled, later changed to a county.
idiomatic: Each spring the Liao hunted at Yanfang Marsh; settlers formed a town around the old Huoyin fort, later raised to a county.

literal: Ninety li southeast of the capital.
idiomatic: It stood ninety li southeast of the capital.

literal: Yanfang Marsh spans several hundred li; in spring geese and ducks gather; in summer and autumn many water chestnuts and lotus roots grow.
idiomatic: Yanfang Marsh covers hundreds of li; spring brings geese and ducks; summer and autumn yield water chestnuts and lotus.

literal: When the ruler hunted in spring, guards all wore dark green, each holding linked maces, hawk food, and goose-stabbing awls, lined along the water five or seven paces apart.
idiomatic: For the spring hunt guards wore dark green, spaced five or seven paces along the shore with linked maces, hawk bait, and goose awls.

literal: Upwind they beat drums to startle geese slightly from the water.
idiomatic: Drums upwind startled geese to lift slightly from the water.

literal: The ruler personally loosed eastern-sea green goshawks to seize them.
idiomatic: The ruler himself flew eastern-sea green goshawks to take them.

literal: When a goose fell, fearing the hawk lacked strength, those in line stabbed the goose with belt awls and swiftly took its fat to feed the hawk.
idiomatic: If a goose fell and the hawk might fail, men in line stabbed it with belt awls and hurriedly took its fat for the hawk.

literal: Whoever took the lead goose received silver and silk by rule.
idiomatic: Capturing the lead goose brought a standard reward of silver and silk.

literal: Ruler, imperial clan, and ministers each had allotted grounds.
idiomatic: The ruler, imperial kin, and ministers each held assigned hunting grounds.

literal: Five thousand households.
idiomatic: Five thousand registered households.

literal: Song minister Wang Zeng, Account of Presenting Matters to the Khitan, says: "From Xiongzhou Baima post one crosses the river; forty li to Xincheng County, ancient Dukang Pavilion ground.
idiomatic: Wang Zeng's Account of Service to the Khitan records: "From Xiongzhou's Baima post, forty li by ferry to Xincheng County, the old Dukang Pavilion site.

literal: Another seventy li to Zhuo Prefecture.
idiomatic: Seventy li farther on lies Zhuo Prefecture.

literal: Northward crossing Fan River and Liu-Li River, sixty li to Liangxiang County.
idiomatic: Crossing the Fan and Liu-Li rivers northward, sixty li to Liangxiang County.

literal: Crossing Lugou River, sixty li to Youzhou, styled Yanjing.
idiomatic: Sixty li beyond the Lugou River stands Youzhou, called Yanjing.

literal: The inner city was built against the outer wall's southwest.
idiomatic: The inner city hugged the southwest of the outer ramparts.

literal: Due south is Qixia Gate; within is Yuanhe Hall; east gate is Xuanhe.
idiomatic: The south gate is Qixia; inside stands Yuanhe Hall; the east gate is Xuanhe.

literal: Within the city every ward lane had towers.
idiomatic: Every ward and lane in the city had gate-towers.

literal: There is Minzhong Temple, originally built by Tang Taizong for generals and soldiers who died campaigning against Liaodong;
idiomatic: Minzhong Temple, which Tang Taizong raised for officers and men fallen on the Liaodong campaign;

literal: also Kaitai Temple, built by Prince of Wei Yelü Hanning.
idiomatic: and Kaitai Temple, built by Prince of Wei Yelü Hanning.

literal: Both were sent envoys from the court to visit.
idiomatic: Court envoys were sent to tour both.

literal: Outside the south gate is the Prince of Yu Wang's office, a place for banquets.
idiomatic: South of the gate stands the Prince of Yu's hall, used for feasts.

literal: Outside the gate is Yongping Hostel, formerly named Jieshi Hostel, renamed after the peace treaty.
idiomatic: Beyond the gate is Yongping Hostel, formerly Jieshi Hostel, renamed after the peace accord.

literal: South of it is the Sanggan River.
idiomatic: South lies the Sanggan River.

literal: Shun Prefecture, Guihua Army, middle grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Shun Prefecture—Guihua Army, middle grade, with a prefect.

literal: Qin Shanggu; Han Fanyang; Northern Qi Guidde Commandery territory.
idiomatic: In Qin it was Shanggu; in Han Fanyang; in Northern Qi part of Guidde Commandery.

literal: Sui Kaihuang era: Sumo Mohe fought Goryeo without victory; chief Tudi of the Jueji tribe led several thousand victorious warriors of eight tribes from northwest of Fuyu walled city to submit inward; Shun Prefecture was set to settle them.
idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang, Sumo Mohe lost to Goryeo; Jueji chief Tudi led several thousand warriors of eight tribes from northwest of Fuyu to submit, and Shun Prefecture was founded to receive them.

literal: Tang early Wude changed it to Yan Prefecture; Huichang era changed to Guishun Prefecture; late Tang it remained Shun Prefecture.
idiomatic: Early Tang Wude renamed it Yan Prefecture; in Huichang it became Guishun; by late Tang it was again Shun Prefecture.

literal: There are Wanyu River and Baisui River;
idiomatic: It has the Wanyu and Baisui rivers;

literal: Caowang Mountain, where Cao Cao once encamped; Taigu Valley, where Zou Yan blew the pitch pipes; south of it is Qi's Long Wall.
idiomatic: Caowang Mountain, where Cao Cao once camped; Taigu Valley, where Zou Yan tested pitch pipes; to the south runs Qi's Long Wall.

literal: Northeast of the city are Hualin and Tianzhu two estates; Liao built cool halls—spring for flowers, summer for shade.
idiomatic: Northeast of the city stand the Hualin and Tianzhu estates; the Liao built cool pavilions for spring blossoms and summer shade.

literal: At first the army was called Guining; later renamed.
idiomatic: The army was first called Guining, then renamed.

literal: Governing one county:
idiomatic: It governed one county:

literal: Huairou County.
idiomatic: Huairou County.

literal: Tang Zhenguan year 6 established, administering Wuliu walled town, renamed Shunyi County.
idiomatic: Established in Tang Zhenguan year 6 at Wuliu town, renamed Shunyi County.

literal: Kaiyuan year 4 set Songmo Protectorate Tanhan Prefecture.
idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 4 placed Songmo Protectorate's Tanhan Prefecture here.

literal: Kaibao year 1 changed to Guihua Commandery.
idiomatic: Kaibao year 1 it became Guihua Commandery.

literal: Qianyuan year 1 restored the present name.
idiomatic: Qianyuan year 1 restored the current name.

literal: Five thousand households.
idiomatic: Five thousand registered households.

literal: Miyun County.
idiomatic: Miyun County.

literal: Originally Han Baitan County; Later Han assigned the Jijin Xi.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Baitan County; Later Han placed the Jijin Xi there.

literal: Northern Wei set Miyun Commandery, governing Baitan, Yaoyang, and Miyun three counties.
idiomatic: Northern Wei founded Miyun Commandery over Baitan, Yaoyang, and Miyun counties.

literal: Northern Qi abolished the commandery and two counties; they came under this prefecture.
idiomatic: Northern Qi abolished the commandery and two counties, which then belonged here.

literal: Five thousand households.
idiomatic: Five thousand registered households.

literal: Xingtang County.
idiomatic: Xingtang County.

literal: Originally Ding Prefecture Xingtang County.
idiomatic: Formerly Xingtang County in Ding Prefecture.

literal: Taizu raided Ding Prefecture, broke Xingtang, and drove all its people north to Tan Prefecture, choosing open land to settle them; ten stockades were placed and it was still named Xingtang County.
idiomatic: Taizu raided Ding, took Xingtang, and relocated the entire populace north to Tan Prefecture on open ground; ten stockades were founded and the name Xingtang kept.

literal: Subordinate to Zhangmin Palace.
idiomatic: It answered to Zhangmin Palace.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Fanyang County.
idiomatic: Fanyang County.

literal: Originally Han Zhuo County.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Zhuo County.

literal: Mid-Tang Wude era changed to Fanyang County.
idiomatic: In mid-Tang Wude it was renamed Fanyang County.

literal: There are Zhuo River and Fan River.
idiomatic: The Zhuo and Fan rivers flow there.

literal: Ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

literal: Guan County.
idiomatic: Guan County.

literal: Originally Han Fangcheng County, first belonging to Guangyang State.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Fangcheng County in Guangyang State.

literal: Sui Kaihuang year 9 moved from Yizhou Laishui County to settle here, belonging to Youzhou, taking the Han Guan County name.
idiomatic: Sui Kaihuang year 9 moved the seat from Yizhou Laishui to Youzhou under the old Guan County name.

literal: Tang Wude year 4 belonged to Beiyi Prefecture and the seat moved to Zhangxin Fort.
idiomatic: Tang Wude year 4 it joined Beiyi Prefecture and the administration shifted to Zhangxin Fort.

literal: Zhenguan year 2 Beiyi Prefecture abolished; moved to present administration and again belonged to Youzhou.
idiomatic: Zhenguan year 2 abolished Beiyi and moved the seat here, again under Youzhou.

literal: Ninety li southeast of the prefecture.
idiomatic: Ninety li southeast of the prefectural seat.

literal: Ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

literal: Xincheng County.
idiomatic: Xincheng County.

literal: Originally Han Xinchang County.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Xinchang County.

literal: Tang Dali year 4 split off from Guan County to establish; later abolished.
idiomatic: Tang Dali year 4 carved it from Guan County, then abolished it.

literal: Later Tang Tiancheng year 4 again split from Fanyang County to establish; sixty li south of the prefecture.
idiomatic: Later Tang Tiancheng year 4 carved it again from Fanyang, sixty li south of the prefectural seat.

literal: Ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

literal: Guiyi County.
idiomatic: Guiyi County.

idiomatic: Formerly Han Yi County land.

idiomatic: Under Qi it was merged into Mao County.

literal: Tang Wude year 5 set Beiyi Prefecture; prefecture abolished, county re-established and came under this prefecture.
idiomatic: Tang Wude year 5 created Beiyi Prefecture; when the prefecture fell the county was restored here.

literal: Residents dwell south of the Juma River; administration was at Xincheng in exile.
idiomatic: Households live south of the Juma River with government by proxy at Xincheng.

literal: Four thousand households.
idiomatic: Four thousand registered households.

literal: Yi County.
idiomatic: Yi County.

literal: Twenty-five thousand households.
idiomatic: Twenty-five thousand registered households.

idiomatic: Laishui County.

idiomatic: Sui Kaihuang year 18 renamed it Laishui County.

idiomatic: Forty li east of the prefectural seat.

idiomatic: A Han county first in Zhuo Commandery; its old town lies southwest of Xiong Prefecture.

idiomatic: Tang Wude year 5 it joined Beiyi Prefecture.

idiomatic: Under Tang it was Youzhou; Kaiyuan year 18 created Ji Prefecture.

idiomatic: Baoqiu River flows there.

literal: Four thousand households.

idiomatic: Sanhe County.

idiomatic: Year 8 it belonged to Ying Prefecture.

literal: Year 11 again belonged to Youzhou.
idiomatic: Year 11 it was again under Youzhou.

literal: Year 18 came under this prefecture.
idiomatic: Year 18 it came under this prefecture.

literal: In Search of the Supernatural: "Yong Bo of Luoyang was filial; after his parents died he buried them on Wuzhong Mountain.
idiomatic: Search of the Supernatural records: "Yong Bo of Luoyang, filial, buried his parents on Wuzhong Mountain.

literal: The mountain is eighty li high with no water above; Yong Bo set out drink.
idiomatic: The peak rises eighty li without water above; Yong Bo set out drink.

literal: Whoever came to drink received a peck of stone; planting produced jade, hence the name Yutian.
idiomatic: Travelers who drank received a peck of stone; planting it yielded jade, whence the name Yutian.

idiomatic: Jing Prefecture—Qing'an Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

idiomatic: Formerly Zunhua County in Ji Prefecture; founded in the Chongxi era.

idiomatic: Luan Prefecture lies against mountains and rivers, a strategic hinge between the northern marches and the Han heartland.

literal: There is Fusu Spring, very sweet; Qin crown prince Fusu, building the Long Wall northward, once encamped here;

idiomatic: Linyu Mountain rises in sheer peaks over a thousand ren, looking down on the Yu River.

literal: Huangluo River emerges north from Lulong Mountain and flows south into Ru River.
idiomatic: Huangluo River issues north from Lulong Mountain and runs south into the Ru River.

literal: Han belonged to Liaoxi Commandery, long abolished.
idiomatic: Under Han it was Liaoxi Commandery, long defunct.

literal: Late Tang entered Khitan rule; Shizong established the county.
idiomatic: Late Tang it passed to the Khitan; Shizong founded the county.

literal: Four thousand households.
idiomatic: Four thousand registered households.

literal: Macheng County.
idiomatic: Macheng County.

literal: Originally Lulong County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Lulong County land.

literal: Tang Kaiyuan year 28 split off a county to open water transport.
idiomatic: Tang Kaiyuan year 28 carved out a county to facilitate river transport.

literal: Northeast is Qianjin smeltery; east is Maoxiang walled town.
idiomatic: Northeast lies Qianjin smeltery; east, Maoxiang town.

literal: Liao split it off to belong to Luan Prefecture.
idiomatic: The Liao detached it to Luan Prefecture.

literal: Forty li southwest of the prefecture.
idiomatic: Forty li southwest of the prefectural seat.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Shicheng County.
idiomatic: Shicheng County.

literal: Han established it, belonging to Youbeiping Commandery, long abolished.
idiomatic: Han founded it in Youbeiping Commandery, long defunct.

literal: Tang Zhenguan era placed Linyu County here; Wansui Tongtian year 1 changed to Shicheng County, thirty li south of Luan Prefecture; Tang Yifeng stone inscription stands there.
idiomatic: Tang Zhenguan placed Linyu County here; Wansui Tongtian year 1 renamed it Shicheng, thirty li south of Luan Prefecture, where a Tang Yifeng inscription remains.

literal: Present county again fifty li farther south; Liao moved the seat to approach the salt office.
idiomatic: The present seat lies fifty li farther south; the Liao relocated it beside the salt monopoly.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.
